item.text: I’m using the earlier input and saved-candidate list from memory to identify distinct omissions, then I’ll write only those additions to `followup.tsv`.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "cat > enrichment/bible/work/s103/discovery/s103-20261009/sec2/luna/followup.tsv <<'EOF'
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Gen.1.14	luminaries mark seasons, days, and years	The commentary joins night/day and dawn/evening and develops seasonal time; Genesis assigns the lights to mark seasons, days, and years, giving the daily pair a wider calendar frame.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Josh.1.8	meditate day and night; do what is written	The commentary links day/night with the people who act rightly; Joshua makes uninterrupted day-and-night meditation the preparation for doing the law, joining the temporal formula to ethical action.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.1.2	meditation on Torah day and night	The commentary treats night/day as linked units and says the ones who endure are those who act rightly; Psalm 1 describes the righteous person meditating on Torah day and night, tying the same cycle to a life of fidelity.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.1.3	fruit in season; leaf does not wither	The commentary connects seasonal time to those who remain standing; Psalm 1's righteous tree bears fruit in its season and does not wither, making endurance a seasonal image.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.55.18	evening, morning, and noon prayer	The commentary names night/day and morning/evening pairs and describes patience across the day; this psalm's speaker prays and is heard at evening, morning, and noon, extending the paired hours into a recurring daily practice.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.74.17	day and night belong to God; lights established	The commentary presents day and night as a joined order; this verse says both belong to God and that God established the lights, grounding the temporal pair in divine ordering.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.74.18	earth's boundaries; summer and winter	The commentary names seasons and treats time as a sequence of joined portions; the next verse says God fixed the earth's boundaries and made summer and winter, connecting cosmic order to seasonal division.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.103.15	human days like grass; flourishing like a field flower	The commentary follows life's stages and says its full span contracts to a brief interval; the psalm compares a person's days to grass and a flower, giving the short lifespan a natural image.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.103.16	wind passes; the place is known no more	The commentary says the long duration of human life collapses and ends in loss; this verse says the wind passes over the flower and it disappears, sharpening the image of erasure.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.103.17	human life contrasted with enduring divine love	The commentary sets human transience against those who remain through faith and right action; the next verse contrasts the fleeting flower with the Lord's steadfast love from everlasting to everlasting.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.121.6	sun by day; moon by night	The commentary joins day and night and says the faithful remain through time; this verse assigns danger by day and night and locates protection across both periods.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Job.7.1	human life as hard service; days like a hired worker	The commentary describes a life passing through stages and ending in a short span; Job's lament asks whether human life is hard service and whether its days are like a hired worker's, adding labor and longing for release to the image of time.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Job.7.6	days swifter than a weaver's shuttle	The commentary says the whole lifetime shrinks to an evening or hour; Job says his days are faster than a weaver's shuttle and end without hope, a specific image of time slipping away.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Eccl.11.6	sow in the morning and keep working at evening	The commentary joins morning to evening and speaks of patience while time passes; Qohelet tells the worker to sow in the morning and not hold back at evening, while admitting the outcome is unknown, joining action to uncertain time.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Lam.3.23	compassions new every morning	The commentary names morning/evening as paired spans and counsels patience; Lamentations says divine mercies are new each morning, making the daily return of morning a ground for hope amid affliction.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Lam.3.25	waiting for the Lord	The commentary explicitly explains sabr as waiting; Lamentations says the Lord is good to those who wait for him and seek him, joining patience to seeking.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Lam.3.26	wait quietly for the Lord's salvation	The commentary links patient waiting to survival through time; Lamentations calls it good to wait quietly for the Lord's salvation, specifying the hoped-for outcome of that waiting.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Hab.2.3	appointed time; wait if the vision seems delayed	The commentary develops fixed seasonal time and glosses sabr as waiting; Habakkuk says the vision has an appointed time and instructs the hearer to wait if it seems delayed, joining a set time to patient expectation.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Dan.12.2	sleepers awake; everlasting life or disgrace	The commentary compresses human time toward the gathering day and speaks of loss; Daniel describes those sleeping in the dust awakening to divergent everlasting outcomes, adding an explicit resurrection horizon.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Dan.12.12	blessing for waiting through a counted span	The commentary says sabr is waiting and the life span contracts to a short interval; Daniel blesses the one who waits and reaches the end of a specified number of days.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Dan.12.13	rest, then stand at the end of days	The commentary joins death, the gathering day, and the fate of those who endure; Daniel is told to go his way, rest, and rise to his allotted place at the end of days, adding a personal resurrection promise.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.26.19	the dead live; dwellers in dust awake	The commentary mentions graves, the gathering day, and the human lifetime ending; Isaiah calls the dead to live and those dwelling in dust to awake, making resurrection an explicit answer to the grave.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.119.160	word is truth; righteous rules endure forever	The commentary pairs haqq with sabr; this verse calls God's word truth and says the righteous ordinances endure forever, directly joining truth with permanence.
strong	tevrat	motif	Shabbat 127a	acts whose fruits are enjoyed now and whose principal remains for the world to come	The commentary names righteous deeds as the answer to loss and describes people helping one another; the Talmud lists concrete acts such as honoring parents, kindness, hospitality, and peacemaking whose reward extends beyond this life.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.24.13	endure to the end and be saved	The commentary says those who attach to one another through patience remain standing; Jesus says the one who endures to the end will be saved, giving patience a clear terminal horizon.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.6.12	inherit promises through faith and patience	The commentary's exception to loss joins faith, righteous action, and sabr; Hebrews urges imitation of those who inherit the promises through faith and patience, aligning endurance with promised outcome.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.10.36	endurance after doing God's will; receive the promise	The commentary couples patience with right action; Hebrews says endurance is needed after doing God's will in order to receive what was promised, making persistence the bridge between action and outcome.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:James.1.3	faith tested produces endurance	The commentary names faith and sabr together; James says the testing of faith produces endurance, giving patience a process rather than treating it as a static trait.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:James.1.4	endurance brought to completion	The commentary says patient persistence carries people through time; James tells endurance to complete its work so that the person may be mature and whole, linking duration to ethical formation.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.8.25	wait patiently for what is not seen	The commentary describes sabr as waiting and directs it toward survival; Paul says hope for what is not seen requires waiting with patience, adding the unseen promise as the object of endurance.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rev.2.10	faithful to death; crown of life	The commentary traces a human span to its end and says the faithful endure; Revelation calls the community to faithfulness even to death and promises the crown of life, linking lifetime's limit to reward.
strong	incil	motif	Didache 16.1	lamps burning; be ready because the hour is unknown	The commentary joins night/day divisions to patience and waiting; the Didache tells its readers to watch their lives, keep lamps lit, and be ready because the Lord's hour is unknown, giving the temporal image an early Christian practice of vigilance.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Job.7.9	cloud vanishes; descent to Sheol does not return	The commentary quotes people who say time destroys them and describes life shrinking toward death; Job's lament says the one who descends to Sheol does not come back, a voice of temporal despair whose placement within Job's complaint keeps it from being a simple doctrinal statement.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Gen.41.49	grain heaped like sea sand across years of plenty	The commentary links accumulated time to survival and recalls the destructive race to amass numbers; Joseph heaps grain during the seven years of plenty to preserve life through famine. The table's ص ب ر / צבר sound correspondence is unverified, and Hebrew means heap rather than the commentary's patience, so this is a contrastive accumulation motif, not a shared sense.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.119.142	righteousness everlasting; Torah is truth	The commentary develops haqq as right/truth; this verse calls God's Torah truth and its righteousness everlasting, joining truth to enduring right order.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Lam.3.22	steadfast love does not cease	The commentary contrasts transient human time with the survival of the faithful; Lamentations grounds hope in the Lord's unfailing compassion, the reason given in the surrounding morning and waiting lines.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Dan.12.13	Daniel's rest and allotted place at the end	The commentary follows a lifetime to its endpoint; this verse tells Daniel to rest and then stand in his allotted place at the end of days, a personal continuation of the resurrection scene.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.6.15	Abraham waited patiently and received the promise	The commentary ties sabr to waiting for an outcome; Hebrews says Abraham patiently endured and obtained the promise, giving a narrative example of long waiting rewarded.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rev.3.10	patient endurance; an approaching hour of testing	The commentary stretches patience across time and reduces the final span to an hour; Revelation connects keeping the word of endurance with preservation from an hour of testing that is coming on the world.
medium	incil	motif	Gospel of Thomas 59	seek the Living One while alive	The commentary emphasizes the shortness of life and its closing encounter; this saying urges seeking the Living One before death, turning limited lifetime into an immediate obligation. English wording varies by translation.
EOF"
